newsitem.title: LIBYA: Libya seeks foreign developers for iron ore.
newsitem.headline: Libya seeks foreign developers for iron ore.

text.p: Libya is seeking foreign developers to help exploit its large-scale iron ore reserves in the southern region of the country to feed its steel mill complex, Libyan industry officials said.

"We call on interested foreign firms to enter into partnership with us to develop the Wadi Shatti iron ore," Mustafa Sed, Technical Director of Libyan Iron and Steel Company (LISC) told Reuters during a visit to the giant manufacturing complex in Misrata, 210 km east of Tripoli.
"It is time for us to use our raw minerals. The (foreign) firms are called to extract them," Sed added. He said LISC currently runs on imported iron ore from Brazil and Sweden.

Sed would not disclose the Wadi Shatti reserves. But European diplomats in Tripoli told Reuters it has an estimated two to three billion tonnes of reserves ranging from 25 percent to 50 percent iron content.
The mine is in the Libyan desert, some 750 km from the coastal city of Misrata.
Sed was talking a few hours before Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi called on Monday night for the privatisation of state-owned industrial firms, including LISC.
No date was set for the implementation of Gaddafi's call and Tripoli-based diplomats said privatisation would need special legislation and studies that might take years.

LISC has a production capacity of 1.3 million tonnes of liquid steel. It was constructed by several foreign firms including Germany's Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG, Austria's Voest-Alpine, Kobe Steel Ltd of Japan, Hyundai Corp of Korea, and Italy's Techint.
It started production in 1988. Some five billion dollars were invested, Libyan officials said.
The plant is powered by the country's cheap gas resources, supplied through a 700-km pipeline linking Misrata to the southern gas fields.
It currently produces concrete-reinforcing bars and rods, light and medium sections, hot-rolled coils and cold-rolled coils.
Sed said that an extension of the factory is being completed and will allow LISC by the third quarter of 1997 to produce hot briquetted iron, hot-dip galvanized coils, and colour-coated coils.
The production is currently exported to European and Arab countries, he added. He said that the complex runs at an average 85 percent of its capacity in liquid steel.
The Misrata's complex has its own port which can accommodate cargo ships of up to 90,000 tonnes capacity, and a power and desalination plant.
It covers 1,200 hectares and has some 5,600 workers, 90 percent of whom are Libyan nationals.
